vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: agent-chronicle
Version: 0.6.3

The agent-chronicle skill is a legitimate utility designed to help AI agents maintain a reflective diary. The code gathers context from local session logs and persistent memory files (e.g., quotes.md, decisions.md) to generate journal entries using a sub-agent pattern (sessions_spawn). The export scripts (export.py and export_pdf.py) use pandoc and WeasyPrint to generate documents, notably employing the --sandbox flag for pandoc to mitigate execution risks. No evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, or harmful prompt injection was found; the logic is entirely consistent with the stated purpose of AI self-reflection.

llm.summary: Agent Chronicle's code and instructions are coherent with its stated purpose (an agent-facing diary): it reads/writes the agent's memory files and spawns sub-agents for generation; nothing requested is disproportionate — but there are a few practical/privacy notes to review before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (AI diary) align with required binaries and included scripts: the skill is Python-based and reads/writes 'memory' files to build diary entries, persists quote/curiosity/decision files, and emits tasks for OpenClaw's sessions_spawn. No unrelated cloud credentials or other service keys are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and scripts explicitly direct the agent to read session logs (memory/YYYY-MM-DD.md) and persistent diary files (quotes.md, curiosity.md, decisions.md, relationship.md). This is expected for a diary but means the skill will collect and include conversational content and any sensitive data present in those logs when generating entries. It does not read unrelated system files or hidden credentials in the codebase.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec (instruction-only) which lowers risk; local Python scripts are included. Export relies on external binaries/libraries (pandoc subprocess call; export_pdf requires WeasyPrint and python-markdown). Export HTML uses a remote CSS URL (https://cdn.simplecss.org/simple.min.css) that pandoc may fetch; this is benign but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no secrets or API keys. It uses optional environment variables OPENCLAW_WORKSPACE or AGENT_WORKSPACE to locate the workspace; otherwise it searches common directories. One minor oddity: the bundled config.json has diary_path set to '/root/clawd/memory/diary/' — a hardcoded absolute path that may be unintended and should be reviewed/adjusted before use.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill is not force-included. The skill can be invoked autonomously (default) which is normal for skills. Auto-generation is an optional config the user must enable; the skill does write files into the agent's memory workspace (expected behavior for a diary).
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: create diary entries by reading your agent's session logs and diary files and (when configured) appending summaries to daily memory. Before installing, check these points: 1) Privacy: the skill will read conversational logs (memory/*.md) and may include their content in generated diaries — remove or redact any secrets/sensitive text from those logs or disable memory_integration if you’re concerned. 2) Config path: inspect and edit config.json (the shipped file points to /root/clawd/memory/diary/) so entries are stored where you expect and with appropriate permissions. 3) Autosave/auto-generate: keep 'auto_generate' disabled unless you want periodic autonomous writes. 4) Export tools: exporting to PDF/HTML requires external tools (pandoc, or WeasyPrint + python-markdown); ensure you install these from trusted sources. 5) Review file writes: setup.py will create files in the configured diary path; ensure the agent process has only the intended write access. If you want higher assurance, run the scripts in a sandboxed environment and review generated entries and the emitted sub-agent task JSON before allowing sub-agent spawning.
